claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch without a material weakness disclosure is compliant and adequately supported because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and remaining segment-specific risk can be handled through documentation and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification and disclosure.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Non-core or low-volume product labels do not resolve materiality when named commitments are affected.
Open legal review and missing approved risk acceptance weigh against a compliant finding.
Public best-practice guidance can support monitoring and documentation, but it cannot replace required internal policy support.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the multilingual support gap must be disclosed before launch.
Any approved risk-acceptance record expressly covering this gap for the named customer commitments or launch use cases.
The exact text of the two regional support commitments naming the affected segment.
The underlying evaluation record showing the 1.1 percentage point miss and the applicable threshold.
The proposed model card or launch disclosure text, if any, showing how this limitation would be communicated.
Any internal materiality determination memo applying the stated policy to this specific segment gap.
specific_concerns: The available summary says the multilingual customer support segment misses target by 1.1 percentage points.
The affected segment is named in two regional support commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.

unsupported_claims: That aggregate readiness pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient to establish compliance with the disclosure policy.
